questions.prompt: The newest 19,200 tokens would start with a tool result whose matching call lies just before the cut. What does chooseCut do?
options: Moves the cut forward past the tool result, so the call and its result are summarized together
Keeps the tool result and drops its call
Moves the cut back to include the call, ignoring the retain budget
Deletes the tool result from the log
questions.explanation: A kept history must never start with a result whose request is gone. chooseCut advances the cut past tool messages, so call and result stay together.

questions.prompt: Why does the summary request send the history unchanged and put the instruction as the last user message?
options: Because the model cannot read system messages
So the request begins exactly like earlier ones and the provider can reuse its work for that prefix
So the summary includes the instruction text
Because the template must come before the history
questions.explanation: Reuse stops at the first differing token. Replaying the same history and adding the instruction at the end keeps the beginning identical.

questions.prompt: A session is compacted a second time. What should happen to the first summary?
options: It is copied forward unchanged above the new one
It is deleted without being read
It is merged into a single new summary, keeping facts that are still true
questions.explanation: The old summary sits inside the summarized range, marked by <compacted-summary> tags. The instruction asks the model to merge it, so summaries do not pile up.
